Citizenship

Kiswahili: Uraia

Outlines rights and duties of Kenyan citizens, acquisition of citizenship by birth or registration, dual citizenship rights, and retention of nationality.

Key constitutional takeaways

  • •Every citizen is entitled to the rights, privileges, and benefits of citizenship.
  • •Dual citizenship is explicitly permitted for citizens by birth.
  • •Kenyan citizenship cannot be lost by reason only of marriage or dissolution of marriage.

Articles in Chapter 3

Select an article to read its legal clauses and plain language meaning.

Clauses

(1)Every citizen is entitled to- (a) the rights, privileges and benefits of citizenship, subject to the limits provided or permitted by this Constitution; and (b) a Kenyan passport and any document of registration or identification issued by the State to citizens.
(2)A passport or other document referred to in clause (1)(b) may be denied, suspended or confiscated only in accordance with an Act of Parliament that satisfies the criteria referred to in Article

In plain language

Every Kenyan has an enforceable constitutional right to identity documents and passports without discrimination.
